title: authorization-assertion-format-and-evidence-bundling-spec
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary:
This page defines a canonical authorization assertion JSON schema and the corresponding rules for bundling and retaining compliance evidence. The goal is to create a single, consistent artifact that operators, auditors, and incident responders can use to reconstruct access decisions and the state necessary to justify them.

Audience:
- Security engineers and compliance owners
- Service owners and platform engineers implementing RBAC and delegation
- SRE and incident response teams responsible for forensic collection

Why this exists:
Disparate services currently emit different fields for authorization checks and evidence. That hampers rapid investigations and increases audit effort. This spec standardizes the minimal assertion shape, evidence attachments, retention windows, and automated bundling workflows.

Scope and non‑scope:
- In scope: internal API access checks, customer-facing token grants, JIT delegation flows, service-to-service role assertions, and privileged session recordings.
- Out of scope: source control commits and developer IDE telemetry (covered by SDLC secure build artifacts).

1) Authorization assertion: canonical schema
Provide the following JSON as the canonical runtime assertion that must be logged by any service performing a decision that will be considered audit‑grade. Services may add additional vendor-specific keys but must not remove or rename the core fields below.

Required top-level fields (described in plain text):
- assertion_id: stable UUID v4 for this decision event
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601 UTC timestamp when the decision occurred
- decision: allow | deny | conditional
- principal: object-id for caller (user:alice, svc:billing-api, sa:job-runner)
- principal_type: human | service | machine_account
- resource: canonical resource identifier (arn-like or URL)
- action: operation attempted (read, write, execute, token:exchange, impersonate)
- policy_version: policy id and semantic version used to make the decision (e.g., policy-acct-123@v2.1.0)
- reason_code: short code mapping to a policy path or rule id (e.g., RBAC-ALLOW-023)
- confidence: numeric 0..100 representing confidence in input signals (optional for conditional decisions but recommended)

Suggested optional fields (strongly recommended):
- request_context_id: correlation id that can be cross-walked to trace/span IDs
- client_ip_ipv4: dotted decimal or cidr
- location_hint: region or AZ for geo-aware decisions
- ttl_seconds: if a temporary grant was issued, the grant lifetime

Example assertion JSON (producer log friendly):
```json
{
  "assertion_id": "c1a8f2d8-7b9f-4c3a-9b1a-2d3f4e5a6b7c",
  "timestamp_utc": "2025-07-09T15:22:31Z",
  "decision": "allow",
  "principal": "user:maya.patel",
  "principal_type": "human",
  "resource": "redwood:dedicated:gpu-pool:pool-42:credentials",
  "action": "read",
  "policy_version": "policy-infra-credentials@v1.4.2",
  "reason_code": "RBAC-ALLOW-078",
  "request_context_id": "req-98c3f2ab",
  "client_ip_ipv4": "198.51.100.23",
  "confidence": 94
}
```

2) Evidence bundling model
When a decision is material (defined below), the service must create an evidence bundle JSON file and emit it to the evidence store (see "Storage targets"). The evidence bundle groups the canonical assertion with attachments that provide provenance.

Definition: material decision
A decision is material if any of the following are true:
- the decision allowed access to privileged resources (credential material, key materials, admin APIs)
- the decision was a delegation that created or modified another principal's entitlements
- the decision resulted in a policy override or emergency access (break glass)
- the decision is part of a regulation-bound customer workflow (e.g., EU data export, HIPAA access)

Evidence bundle shape (single file JSON):
- bundle_id: UUID - matches assertion_id if single decision, otherwise new bundle id grouping multiple assertions
- assertions: list of assertion_id (one or more)
- attachments: list of attachment descriptors (see below)
- collected_by: service or agent name that assembled the bundle
- collected_at: timestamp UTC

Attachment descriptor fields:
- name: short name (credential-snapshot.json, session-recording.mp4)
- type: json | text | binary | key_material | video | image
- storage_uri: s3/gs/az blob path or internal artifact id
- hash_sha256: hex string for integrity verification
- retention_class: short label mapping to retention policy (ephemeral, standard, longterm, legal-hold)

Example bundle outline:
```json
{
  "bundle_id": "bndl-5f9e1a33-2d4f-4c7f-bd6b-1a2e3b4c5d6f",
  "assertions": ["c1a8f2d8-7b9f-4c3a-9b1a-2d3f4e5a6b7c"],
  "attachments": [
    {"name":"policy-snapshot.json","type":"json","storage_uri":"s3://evidence-prod/2025/07/09/policy-snap-...","hash_sha256":"...","retention_class":"standard"},
    {"name":"session-log.txt","type":"text","storage_uri":"s3://evidence-prod/2025/07/09/session-...","hash_sha256":"...","retention_class":"ephemeral"}
  ],
  "collected_by":"authz-agent-1",
  "collected_at":"2025-07-09T15:22:45Z"
}
```

3) Retention classes and mapping rules
This section defines retention_class labels and the mapping to storage and lifecycle rules. The mapping must be enforced by the evidence ingestion pipeline and enforced by the retention manager job.

Retention classes:
- ephemeral: 30 days. Small footprint evidence (request headers, temporary token raw)
- standard: 2 years. Routine access decisions for most services and customers
- longterm: 7 years. Financial, contractual, and critical security-control decisions
- legal-hold: indefinite until released by Legal and CISO

Storage targets:
- ephemeral -> evidence-prod/ephemeral/...
- standard -> evidence-prod/standard/...
- longterm -> evidence-archive/longterm/...
- legal-hold -> evidence-archive/holds/...

Retention enforcement rules (examples):
1. All bundles tagged ephemeral are purged by the retention manager after 30 days; purge job must record purge_event to the audit index.
2. Any bundle referenced by an open incident (status open) is escalated to legal-hold automatically until the incident is closed and legal approves release.
3. Longterm artifacts are archived to a WORM-capable store with replication across two regions.

4) Evidence ingestion and signing
- Services must push evidence bundles to the evidence ingestion API within 5 seconds of creation for synchronous flows, or within 1 minute for async flows.
- The ingestion API validates the bundle signature (HMAC) and stores a manifest with the first-seen timestamp.
- The ingestion API returns a stable evidence_id which must be referenced in the originating request trace.

CLI example:
```bash
curl -X POST https://evidence-ingest.redwood.example/v1/bundles \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EVIDENCE_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -F "bundle=@mybundle.json" \
  -F "signature=sha256=..."
```

5) Forensics and incident response usage
Minimum checklist to support rapid reconstruction (ordered):
1. Collect the evidence bundle(s) associated with assertion_id(s) and all linked traces (request_context_id).
2. Retrieve the policy_version artifact and the exact policy text referenced in the bundle.
3. If delegation occurred, collect change history for the delegated entitlement (who, when, revoked?).
4. Capture session recordings or stdout dumps tied to the decision.
5. Snapshot the principal's active entitlements at the time of decision (cache or directory snapshot).

Investigation tip: when confidence < 50 or decision==conditional, prioritize raw input signals (token claims, identity provider assertions) as they often contain transient attributes used in the decision.

6) Automation rules and example workflows
A. Auto-promotion to legal-hold when the decision touches PII for EU customers:
- Detection: policy tag contains 'gdpr:personal_data' -> evidence bundle retention_class := legal-hold; create a JIRA ticket to Legal with evidence_id.

B. Emergency break-glass flow evidence bundling:
- Operator uses the "emergency-access" endpoint which returns a temporary grant. The endpoint must create an evidence bundle with an immediate attachment of operator justification (text/plain) and operator session recording (binary), then set retention_class=longterm and notify SOC.

7) Operational requirements and SLOs
- Ingestion latency: 95th percentile < 1s for synchronous bundles after arrival at ingestion endpoint.
- Integrity verification: 100% of bundles must have valid hash_sha256 for each attachment; exceptions must be flagged and quarantined.
- Traceability: 99.9% of assertions must contain request_context_id that maps to our tracing system. Missing correlations generate an automated monitoring alert.

8) Roles and ownership
- Policy authors: product-security owning policy_versioning and compatibility testing.
- Evidence ingestion: infra-security (on-call rota) and evidence-ops.
- Retention manager: compliance team (legal handoff) + infra for enforcement.

9) Implementation checklist for services
1. Emit canonical assertion with required fields at each decision point.
2. On material decision, call evidence-assembly agent to collect attachments and produce bundle.
3. Push bundle to ingestion API and record returned evidence_id in trace and local logs.
4. Tag bundle with retention_class using the rules above or via policy-driven classification API.
5. Monitor ingestion success / failure metrics and alert on >0.1% failure rate per day.

10) Example small JSON schema for assertion (OpenAPI fragment for implementers):
```yaml
components:
  schemas:
    AuthorizationAssertion:
      type: object
      required:
        - assertion_id
        - timestamp_utc
        - decision
        - principal
        - principal_type
        - resource
        - action
        - policy_version
        - reason_code
      properties:
        assertion_id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        timestamp_utc:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        decision:
          type: string
          enum: [allow, deny, conditional]
        principal:
          type: string
        principal_type:
          type: string
          enum: [human, service, machine_account]
        resource:
          type: string
        action:
          type: string
        policy_version:
          type: string
        reason_code:
          type: string
        request_context_id:
          type: string
        client_ip_ipv4:
          type: string
        confidence:
          type: integer
          minimum: 0
          maximum: 100
```
Appendices:
A. Example retention mapping matrix (text table):
- Request headers (ephemeral) | session logs (standard) | policy text (standard) | credential dumps (longterm) | break-glass recordings (legal-hold)

B. Frequently asked questions (short):
Q: Can services add fields to the assertion?
A: Yes, but core fields must remain present and semantically equivalent. Additional fields should be namespaced (x-redwood-...).

Q: Who approves a legal-hold release?
A: Legal + CISO signoff via the Evidence Manager UI.

Caveats and future work:
- This spec focuses on the payload shape and lifecycle rules. Future phases will specify richer normative policy tagging, automated classification ML, and a RBAC certification harness to reduce false positives for legal-hold triggers.
